page: Google Cloud Platform m4-megamem-56 is an x86_64 architecture instance belonging to the Memory Optimized server family. The configuration provisions 56 dedicated vCPUs alongside 744.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of approximately 13.29 GB of RAM per virtual CPU core. This high memory-to-core ratio is designed specifically for workloads requiring massive RAM footprints to maintain low-latency in-memory data processing.

Hardware resource composition lacks local storage disks and discrete graphics acceleration, offering 0.0 GPUs and no bundled local storage volumes. Storage must be provisioned via remote block storage interfaces. Additionally, the instance provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating existing network infrastructure or allocated network resources for external routing.

From a cost efficiency and architectural perspective, m4-megamem-56 concentrates financial investment on memory density. The instance trades away local NVMe I/O and accelerator support in favor of a vast continuous memory space. This profile aligns directly with large in-memory databases, enterprise in-memory caching solutions, large-scale ETL pipelines, and data-intensive analytics that exceed the capacities of standard compute-balanced configurations.
description: Google Cloud Platform m4-megamem-56 is a memory-optimized server configuration based on the x86_64 architecture. The server includes no integrated local storage or hardware GPU accelerators, directing operational focus entirely to large-scale host memory access while external network volumes handle persistence. Network connectivity operates without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Qualitative cost efficiency centers on high memory density, making the instance a dedicated solution for enterprise workloads where memory footprint dictates scaling requirements. Typical deployments include in-memory databases, distributed caches, intensive extract-transform-load (ETL) routines, and large-scale data science operations.
